title: DenseOpenFinitenessComparison
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field and P=(X,A) a curve coefficient pair [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting] with constructible torsion abelian sheaf A [def-weil-pbc-constructible-torsion]. Let U be a dense open of X, j its inclusion, and B=j_!j^*A [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Use the coefficient equivalence E from abelian groups to modules over ULift Z, defined by the inverse of the forgetful equivalence from Z-modules followed by restriction of scalars along ULift Z ≃ Z. Put F=E(A) and G=E(B). Write T(F) for the alternative that F has invertible-order torsion or is p-primary for a prime p=char(k) [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion]. C4(G) implies C4(F), and C5(G) implies C5(F). Under T(F) the reverse implications hold as well. Here C4 and C5 are the conditional invertible-order and proper constructible finiteness assertions [def-weil-pbc-C4], [def-weil-pbc-C5].

proof.text:
The reduced closed complement Z is a finite set of k-rational points. In the open-closed
short exact sequence the third term Q = i_* i^* F has zero positive cohomology and finite
H^0, since its stalks are quotients of the finite constructible stalks of F. In degrees
at least two the first and middle terms have isomorphic cohomology. In degrees zero and
one the exact sequence is 0 → H^0(G) → H^0(F) → H^0(Q) → H^1(G) → H^1(F) → 0.
For either proper constructible finiteness or invertible-order constructible finiteness,
this exact sequence transfers finiteness from G to F: subgroups, quotients and extensions
of finite groups are finite. In the reverse direction it transfers finiteness from F
to G by the same argument and the finite H^0(Q). Constructibility of F is the assumption
hP, transported to the module coefficient encoding. For invertible-order finiteness in
the reverse direction, if F is primary and G has invertible order then G is zero by
stalk conservativity; otherwise the assumed torsion alternative gives invertible order
of F. All arguments apply to empty Z and the zero sheaf.
